note: The review council's table: `default_council` is the reviewers that run when none is named by `--reviewer` or a council.json file, and a harness with no entry there needs a model named. One row per reviewer harness; each entry of `argv` is one flag with its reason and its source. An entry with `when` is used only if that condition holds (`api_key`: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set; `!api_key`: it is not; `budget`: --budget-usd is given; `effort`: the reviewer names an effort). `listed_in_help` says that the installed tool's own --help named the flag on the `read` day, at the `help_version`. `run` is `tested` only where a harmless run showed the effect, else `UNVERIFIED`; `observed` says what a run showed and on which day, also for an entry that stays `UNVERIFIED` because the run did not try its effect. `max_prompt` lists the input limits of a harness; `review council` uses the first row that applies (`platform`: a `sys.platform` prefix; `programs`: the extensions of the program that would start) and checks the assembled prompt against it before the plan is shown and again before each reviewer starts. A row gives the `limit`; its `unit` (`characters`, counted as Unicode code points, `utf-16` code units, or UTF-8 `bytes`); what it `measure`s (`prompt`, the prompt alone; `command line`, the Windows command line with its final NUL; `arguments and environment`, every argument and environment string with its NUL and pointer); the `version` it was read for; its `source`; and the `read` day. A harness or platform with no row that applies has no limit checked, and the plan says so. The model ids are examples: a model name changes faster than this file, and a reviewer entry on the command line overrides it.
